message.content:
You are working in the deepseek-harness repository (a git worktree of branch `claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt`). Read `AGENTS.md`, `packages/AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/defensive-patterns.md`, and `.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md` before changing anything. Commit on the worktree branch as you go (small, well-described commits); do not push and do not open a pull request. Never put model names or identifiers of the model you are running on in any committed artifact. Every commit message ends with these two trailer lines: `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>` and `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HEXjzxR7CyMizem5kFAB4C`.

## The defect you are fixing

The Proving Ground bench (`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/`) runs cells through `dsh-fleet` / `dsh-experiments` over `dsh-environment-runner`. Every cell's workspace is created as a sibling directory under the run directory (`<run>/cell-XXXXXX/`), next to the run's `plan.json`, `run.log`, and every other cell. The bench composes the unconfined `@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-local` and no sandbox, at `isolation: none`. A census over the recorded runs under `data/proving-ground/` shows that in every harness-loop run one to five cells ran commands such as `cd <run dir> && cat plan.json run.log && diff cell-A/src/cli.js cell-B/src/cli.js`, one tier-2 cell copied the other repetition's solution (`cp cell-cUuWY2/src/csv.js cell-R8QtdK/src/csv.js`), and one cell wrote a file into a sibling cell's workspace. The persona's instruction not to leave the workspace is not enforcement. Cells implemented by the out-of-process product loop never left their workspace, but nothing enforces that either.

## What to build

1. **Read barrier: a denied ancestor never removes a session's own workspace.** In `packages/verification/read-barrier`, the policy a session resolves to (`ReadBarrierPolicy`) gains the session's own workspace as an explicitly granted directory (derive it from the session's `meta.cwd`; a session without one has no grant). Add a registration API for denied roots scoped to a run (the runner registers a cell's parent directory for the duration of the run and the registration is disposed when the run ends; today `denied` is `root + configuredDenyRoots + protectedRoots`, so extend whichever of these is the right owner, keeping registrations as effects with disposers). Document the precedence rule in the package README and JSDoc: a denied root that is an ancestor of the session's granted workspace denies the rest of that ancestor's subtree and leaves the workspace whole.
2. **Enforce the precedence in every path-opening capability the census covers.** `packages/fs/fs-read-barrier` (the fs event gate's containment test must grant the session's workspace before it denies an ancestor), `packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy` (the resolved `SandboxExecutionPolicy` carries the granted workspace beside `deniedReadRoots`), `packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/profiles.ts` (bwrap: mount the denied tmpfs first and re-bind the workspace after it when the denied root is an ancestor of the workspace, keeping the existing order for every other case; Landlock: `carveGrant` must keep a grant root whose ancestor is denied, granting the root itself while `carveGrant('/', denied)` still excludes the ancestor's subtree; Seatbelt: the trailing deny clause must be followed by an allow for the workspace, or whatever that dialect needs so a later form outranks the deny), and the search spawn if it resolves the policy separately. Prove each with unit tests, including the tiny cases: denied root equals the workspace's parent, equals a grandparent, equals the workspace itself (then nothing is granted), and a denied root inside the workspace (existing behavior, still denied).
3. **Runner: a cell reads nothing above its workspace.** In `packages/improvement/environment-runner`, every run registers `dirname(request.workspace)` as a denied root for its session when a read barrier is composed, disposes the registration at the end of the run, and records a `read-barrier/denied` count on the run report so the scorekeeper can carry it. Without a composed barrier behavior is unchanged (isolation none, unenforced). Extend `packages/improvement/scorekeeper` facts and rows with the per-cell count of denied reads (name it precisely, e.g. `escapesDenied`), and the observatory column set if rows are shown there.
4. **Bench and district compositions confine the harness loop.** In `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/cordis.yml` and its overlays, replace `dsh-bash-local` with the sandbox stack the `read-barrier-process` fixture composes (`dsh-sandbox-local`, `dsh-sandbox-policy` in `workspace-write` mode, `dsh-bash-sandbox`, `dsh-read-barrier`, `dsh-fs-read-barrier`, and the existing fs tools). The bench keeps `isolation: none` in its base composition because the E2 candidate arm delegates to an out-of-process product provider, which the runner refuses under any higher claim; add an overlay `overlays/route-only.cordis.yml` that patches the runner to `isolation: process` for compositions whose arms are all on the session's own route. Keep the village-live district composition working (it delegates every cell to the product, so it stays at `none`; confine its cell agents' bash anyway). Verify with `pnpm run verify-cordis-config` and the bench's keyless e2e (`examples/headless-agent/tests/proving-ground-bench.e2e.ts`), and add an e2e in the proving-ground-bench or environment-run fixture that proves, with the real sandbox on this Linux host (bwrap is at /usr/bin/bwrap; the Landlock addon `@deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run` may or may not be installed, so select whichever runner `dsh-sandbox-local` resolves, and skip cleanly with a named reason only when neither is available), that a cell's `bash` cannot list or read its parent directory or a sibling cell while it can read and write its own workspace, and that the denied attempt is logged as `read-barrier/denied` and counted on the report.
5. **Census as a tool.** Add `data/proving-ground/tools/census-escapes.mjs` (or extend `record-run.mjs`) so a recorded run reports, per cell, tool calls that name a path above the cell's workspace or another cell id, and the count of `read-barrier/denied` events; `record-run.mjs` prints the census with the record. Run it over every existing record under `data/proving-ground/` and add one paragraph to `data/proving-ground/README.md` (and its `.zh.md`, then re-record the pairing with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write data/proving-ground/README.md`) before the runs table, stating that records dated before this slice ran unconfined in a sibling layout, giving the per-record counts of cells that read the run directory or a sibling and the two cases of copying and writing, and that later records run confined. Do not rewrite the existing record paragraphs.
6. **Agent Note** (bilingual triplet, `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-08-sealed-cell-workspace.md` + `.zh.md` + `.i18n.yaml`, format enforced by `verify-agent-note-format`: line 1 `# Agent Note: <title>`, line 3 `Status: proposed`, line 5 the language line, sections `## Problem`, `## Proposal`, bespoke sections, `## Alternatives considered`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Risks`): the defect, the census numbers, the precedence rule, why the parent is denied rather than each sibling (listing the run directory or reading plan.json also leaks the experiment to the model), why the product arm stays unconfined and how it is audited instead, and what every earlier record's reading loses.

## Gates before you finish

`pnpm exec tsc -b tsconfig.host.json`, `pnpm exec tsx scripts/run-oxlint.ts <changed .ts files>`, focused vitest runs for every package you touch with per-file 100% coverage (`pnpm run test:coverage -- <paths>` or the package's own coverage run), `pnpm run doc-sync` (bilingual triplets re-recorded with `verify-translation-pairing --write`), and the keyless e2e files you touched. Update every affected README (package READMEs document config keys and error codes; `docs/subsystems/` pages where the read barrier and sandbox are described). Report at the end: what changed, the census table, the gate results with commands, and anything you could not do and why.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- dsh-archive-agent-notes: Use when adding, auditing, pruning, archiving, restoring, or reviewing Agent Notes in deepseek-harness; checks every new note for superseded active records, classifies implemented notes by future decision value, deletes rejected notes that no longer prevent a tempting fallacy, and applies the frozen archived/{kind} triplet and manifest rules.
- dsh-code-review: Use when reviewing a pull request in the deepseek-harness repo — orients the reviewer to this codebase's standards (AGENTS.md conventions, defensive patterns, ADRs, quality gates) and the review-specific checks that code alone can't show
- dsh-doc-site-sync: Use when publishing, updating, moving, or removing DeepSeek Harness documentation website pages; editing website/docs.ts mappings or navigation; diagnosing a page missing from the VitePress site; fixing projected documentation links; or running the docs:dev, docs:check, and doc-sync workflow after website-content changes.
- dsh-doc-standards: Use when writing, moving, reviewing, or auditing documentation in the deepseek-harness repo — choosing hierarchy and detail, separating tutorials from references, checking tutorial progression, trimming doc slop, responding to a verify-doc-budgets failure, or requests like "improve the docs", "audit the docs", "where should this be documented", or "this doc is too long".
- dsh-find-simplifications: Use when working in the deepseek-harness repo to find non-obvious simplification candidates, write proposed Agent Notes or inline TODO/FIXME/XXX notes, audit or coalesce superseded Agent Notes, or fold worthwhile simplification ideas from another PR; especially for dead, duplicated, speculative, over-built, added-then-removed, or hand-rolled-where-a-dependency-exists surfaces.
- dsh-merging-stacked-prs: Use when landing a stack of dependent GitHub PRs (A ← B ← C, where each bases on the one below) onto master, merging a PR whose base is another open PR's branch, or whenever a request mentions "stacked PRs", "PR stack", "dependent PRs", or merging several related PRs in sequence. Requires every same-repository dependency chain to use GitHub's official stacked-PR feature before landing so GitHub owns stack-wide rules, CI, ordering, retargeting, and merge state.
- dsh-pre-push-checks: Use before pushing, force-pushing, marking ready for review, or claiming checks pass on a deepseek-harness branch, and immediately after gh stack sync publishes rewritten branches, to select the smallest tests and checks that cover the outgoing or just-published diff without reflexively running the full repository suite.
- dsh-prose-standard: Use when writing, reviewing, restoring, trimming, or auditing prose in the deepseek-harness repo, including deciding where documentation or comments are required across Markdown, JSDoc, code and test comments, prompts, descriptions, diagnostics, and CLI or UI strings.
- dsh-trim-cot-leakage: Use when auditing or fixing prose that reads like a leaked reasoning transcript — dead design-session citations such as (decision N), audit item codes, or §N of uncommitted drafts; change narration such as "used to", "no longer", "this cut"; stack or review vantage ("a later PR in this stack", "rejected in review"); reviewer-addressed justifications; control-flow narration; or hedged planning residue in comments, JSDoc, docs, or Agent Notes.
- record-browser-gif: Record browser or Web UI interaction demos as optimized GIFs using the available built-in browser, state-based frame capture, and deterministic encoding, then publish to a dedicated assets branch when the task includes attaching the GIF to a pull request. Use when asked to make, record, or generate a GIF that demonstrates a browser workflow, and for every pull request that changes product-user-visible GUI behavior, which MUST include a GIF recorded from the pull request's real server and model flow.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` without a compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities
python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
data/        this repository's own transcripts, runs, knowledge packs (see data/README.md)
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and residue of deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns it
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; merge only after checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, real-API e2e for providers.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.

91	- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, real-API e2e for providers.
92	- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or an irreducibly repository-wide change.
93	- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).
94	
95	## Secrets / .env
96	
97	Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). 98	
99	## Conventions
100	
101	- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
102	- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
103	- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
104	- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
105	- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
106	- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
107	- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
108	- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
109	- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
110	- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
111	- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
112	- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
113	- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
114	- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
115	- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
116	- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
117	- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
118	- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
119	- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
120	- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
121	- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
122	- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
123	- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
124	- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
125	- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
126	- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
127	- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
128	- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
129	- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
130	- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.
131	
132	## Defensive patterns
133	
134	Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.
135	
136	## Type safety and documentation
137	
138	Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.
139	
140	Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.
141	
142	Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.
143	
144	## Editing these instructions
145	
146	`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when required content genuinely needs the space.
147	
148	## Vendoring policy
149	
150	`vendor/` packages are pinned source copies (manifest with upstream SHAs in [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)). Update via its sync procedure; re-apply or retire logged local modifications; rerun `pnpm run test && pnpm run build`.

## alphaXiv
alphaXiv provides access to a database of over 2.5 million academic research papers from arXiv. (computer science, mathematics, physics, statistics, quantitative biology/finance, electrical engineering, NOT biomedical, clinical, or life science papers from PubMed, Cell, Nature) These tools are useful when the user asks about, references, or discusses academic papers, scientific research, scholarly literature, citations, research topics, or anything related to academic work. If the user mentions a research area, methodology, scientific concept, asks for literature reviews, wants to find related work, or asks questions that could benefit from academic sources, consider using the search tools. When the user references a specific paper or asks about its content, the paper content and PDF query tools can help. Prefer searching for and citing real papers over relying on memory alone for research questions. The library tools manage the user's own folders of bookmarked papers: a paper can live in several folders at once, and 'to read', 'reading', and 'completed' are just the default folders rather than exclusive states. The researcher tools answer questions about people: who works on a subject, an organization's roster, where someone is now, who they publish with, and the user's own follows. Results address papers as [ID=<id>] and researchers as [SLUG=<slug>]; pass those values back to the tools that take a paper id or a researcher slug, and render them as https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/<id> and https://www.alphaxiv.org/@<slug> rather than showing the bracketed handle to the user.

## Anthropic_Economic_Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

## Firecrawl
Firecrawl provides web, developer, and research search. Use firecrawl_search to find relevant results across the web and specialized indexes. For a programming question, firecrawl_developer_search searches indexed repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and curated documentation sites and returns the matched passages, and skills: "only" narrows it to agent-skill files; firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"] reaches the same index beside ordinary web results, returning the hits in the web group rather than as passages and offering no skills filter. For a biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature question, the firecrawl_research_* tools search the paper index, while categories: ["research"] on firecrawl_search filters ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites. Use the firecrawl_research_* tools to search academic and research literature, expand from anchor papers via the citation graph, and read full-text passages from a specific paper. All tools are read-only and return ranked results.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Hugging_Face
Hugging Face Hub MCP server for models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, and docs.
Prefer this connector's live Hub capabilities over the public website for all configured listings such as today's trending models, the current model leaderboard, daily papers, and paper popularity.

Use hf_fs for Hub filesystem and discovery:
- trending models: ls hf://models/trending
- trending datasets or Spaces: ls hf://datasets/trending, ls hf://spaces/trending
- trending papers / daily papers / paper of the day: ls hf://papers/trending, ls hf://papers/daily/latest
- search models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, or docs: search hf://models QUERY
- read a known file: cat hf://models/OWNER/NAME/README.md

Other advertised Hub tools can search or inspect a known repo id. Use hf_whoami for the current Hugging Face account.

hf:// URIs can be converted to browser URLs by replacing hf://buckets/OWNER/NAME/PATH with https://huggingface.co/buckets/OWNER/NAME/resolve/PATH; for models, datasets, and spaces, use https://huggingface.co[/datasets|/spaces]/OWNER/NAME/resolve/main/PATH. URL-encode each path segment.

arXiv paper ids (for example 2502.16161) are often used as references between datasets, models, and papers. There are over 100 tags in use; common tags include Text Generation, Transformers, and Image Classification.
Hugging Face tools are being used by authenticated user 'LBJLincoln26'

## Supabase
Here are guidelines for using Supabase tools effectively:

- Before making schema changes, use `list_tables` to understand the existing structure
- When debugging issues, start with `get_logs` and `get_advisors` before making changes
- Use `get_project_url` and `get_publishable_api_key` when helping users configure client-side integrations

If you have access to a local development environment with a filesystem and shell:
- Install the Supabase agent skill for critical development and security guidance: `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/ai-skills.md)
- Use the Supabase CLI (`supabase`) for local development workflows such as starting a local stack, managing migrations, and running edge functions locally (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development.md)
- Prefer local development and testing before applying changes to a remote project

If you are running in a web-only or remote environment without filesystem or shell access:
- Rely on the MCP tools directly for all Supabase interactions
- Use `apply_migration` carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).

- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. 64	     * capability. Log-only — it never enters model history.

124	 * every one it was given. Every declared authority is denied to a role in

192	/** The attestation file's decision inputs, read once per verification. */
193	export interface AttestationFile {
194	  /** Numeric owner reported by `stat`. */
195	  readonly uid: number
196	  /** Permission bits reported by `stat`. */
197	  readonly mode: number
198	  /** Whether the path resolves to a regular file. */
199	  readonly isFile: boolean
200	  /** SHA-256 hex digest of the file's bytes. */
201	  readonly sha256: string
202	}

204	/**
205	 * Why `file` does not prove another operating-system account wrote the
206	 * attestation, or `undefined` when it does. The property the `host` level
207	 * asserts is exactly this: an in-process component cannot produce such a file
208	 * without already holding another account's privileges.
209	 * @param file - the attestation file's owner, mode, kind, and digest.
210	 * @param effectiveUid - this process's effective uid; absent on a platform without one.
211	 * @returns the human-readable problem, or undefined when the file verifies.
212	 */
213	export function attestationProblem(file: AttestationFile, effectiveUid: number | undefined): string | undefined {
214	  if (!file.isFile) return 'is not a regular file'
215	  if (effectiveUid === undefined) return 'cannot be attributed to an operating-system owner on this platform'
216	  if (file.uid === effectiveUid) return `is owned by this harness account (uid ${String(effectiveUid)})`
217	  if ((file.mode & FOREIGN_WRITABLE_BITS) !== 0) {
218	    return `is writable outside its owner (mode ${(file.mode & 0o777).toString(8)})`
219	  }
220	  return undefined
221	}

270	 * @returns the expanded absolute path.

273	function absoluteDirectory(path: string, field: string): string {
274	  const expanded = expandHomePath(path)
275	  if (!isAbsolute(expanded)) {

281	/**
282	 * Create the barrier root owner-only and refuse one another account can read.
283	 *
284	 * POSIX only: Windows has no mode to inspect, so the check is skipped rather
285	 * than faked and the directory's protection there is whatever `mkdir` expresses.
286	 * @param root - the absolute barrier root.
287	 * @throws when the directory exists with group or other permission bits set.
288	 */
289	function createOwnerOnlyRoot(root: string): void {
290	  mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
291	  /* v8 ignore next -- POSIX coverage cannot take the Windows peer; native Windows coverage does. */
292	  if (process.platform === 'win32') return
293	  /* v8 ignore start -- Windows has no POSIX mode enforcement; POSIX behavior tests enforce this peer. */
294	  const mode = statSync(root).mode
295	  if ((mode & GROUP_OTHER_BITS) === 0) return
296	  throw new Error(
297	    `read-barrier: ${root} is readable beyond its owner (mode ${(mode & 0o777).toString(8)});`
298	    + ` run "chmod 700 ${root}" before starting again`,
299	  )
300	  /* v8 ignore stop */
301	}

303	/**
304	 * The read-barrier service (`ctx.readBarrier`). It owns the validator root, the
305	 * per-session reservations that make a session an implementer, and the denied
306	 * set every enforcing capability resolves against.
307	 */
308	export class ReadBarrierService extends Service {
309	  static inject = ['fs']
310	
311	  // Inline schema call: the config catalog walks `static Config` statically.
312	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
313	    // No schema default: the harness home is resolved in the constructor so the
314	    // stored root is always absolute regardless of how it was supplied.
315	    root: z.string(),
316	    denyRoots: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
317	    hostAttestation: z.string(),
318	    isolationClaim: z.union(['none', 'process', 'host'] as const).default('none'),
319	  })

321	  /** The absolute directory the barrier owns; always the first denied directory. */
322	  readonly root: string
323	
324	  /** The isolation this deployment intends to claim, as {@link Config.isolationClaim} set it. */
325	  readonly isolationClaim: ReadBarrierIsolationClaim
326	
327	  /** Absolute directories denied alongside {@link root} by deployment config. */
328	  private readonly configuredDenyRoots: readonly string[]
329	
330	  /** Absolute path of the file an external account writes, absent when none is configured. */
331	  private readonly hostAttestation: string | undefined
332	
333	  /** Registered denied directories, keyed per registration so two registrations of one path both hold. */
334	  private readonly protectedRoots = new Map<object, string>()
335	
336	  /** Reserved run directory per session; holding one is what makes a session the implementer. */
337	  private readonly reservations = new Map<SessionId, string>()
338	
339	  /** Composition a preset roster declared per session; a declared role outranks a reservation. */
340	  private readonly compositions = new Map<SessionId, ReadBarrierComposition>()
341	
342	  /** Capabilities that registered enforcement, keyed per registration so two registrations both hold. */
343	  private readonly enforcing = new Map<object, ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability>()
344	
345	  /**
346	   * Capabilities that enforce by refusing to start, keyed per registration. A
347	   * membership here decides the census entry from {@link isolationClaim} rather
348	   * than from an enforcing listener, because there is no listener to hold.
349	   */
350	  private readonly refusing = new Map<object, ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability>()
351	
352	  /** Why one composed capability enforces nothing, keyed per registration. */
353	  private readonly unenforceable = new Map<object, { capability: ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability; reason: string }>()
354	
355	  /** Sessions whose scope census is already durable, so the census is appended exactly once. */
356	  private readonly censused = new Set<SessionId>()
357	
358	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
359	    super(ctx, 'readBarrier')
360	    this.root = absoluteDirectory(config.root ?? dshHomePath('verification'), 'root')
361	    // schemastery (static Config) already filled `denyRoots`; the cast records
362	    // that runtime fact. `root` has NO schema default, so its fallback to the
363	    // harness home is real branching, resolved absolute either way.
364	    this.configuredDenyRoots = (config.denyRoots as string[]).map(entry => absoluteDirectory(entry, 'denyRoots entry'))
365	    this.hostAttestation = config.hostAttestation === undefined
366	      ? undefined
367	      : absoluteDirectory(config.hostAttestation, 'hostAttestation')
368	    // schemastery (static Config) already filled `isolationClaim`; the cast records that runtime fact.
369	    this.isolationClaim = config.isolationClaim as ReadBarrierIsolationClaim
370	    createOwnerOnlyRoot(this.root)
371	    ctx.on('agent/created', ({ agent }) => { this.installGuard(agent) })
372	    // The census is taken here rather than at creation because a validator
373	    // reserves AFTER the agent exists: the role is settled by the time the
374	    // first request is composed, and this waterfall runs before the loop
375	    // appends that request's `request/header`.
376	    ctx.on('agent/request', async ({ agent }, next) => {
377	      this.recordScope(agent)
378	      return await next()
379	    })
380	    ctx.on('agent/disposed', ({ agent }) => {
381	      // The role belongs to the live session: a disposed agent can no longer
382	      // read, and keeping its reservation would grow the map for a process
383	      // running many environments.
384	      this.reservations.delete(agent.id)
385	      this.compositions.delete(agent.id)
386	      this.censused.delete(agent.id)
387	    })
388	  }

390	  /**
391	   * Mint the run directory for one agent's session and record that session as
392	   * the implementer. The validator writes its standard snapshot, one script per
393	   * check, and any held-out fixture there, so the command line the implementer
394	   * can observe in a process listing names a file whose content it cannot read.
395	   * Reserving the same session twice returns the same directory.
396	   *

398	   * awaited reservation would leave a window in which the session's own reads
399	   * are still unrestricted.

401	   * @returns the absolute run directory, created owner-only.
402	   */
403	  reserve(agent: Agent): string {
404	    const existing = this.reservations.get(agent.id)
405	    if (existing !== undefined) return existing
406	    const directory = join(this.root, RUNS_DIR, agent.id)
407	    mkdirSync(directory, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })

412	  /**

414	   * consumer that reads a reservation asks here rather than through

416	   * implementer, so a reader that reserved to find out would demote the very

419	   * @returns the reserved directory, or `undefined` when the session holds none.

425	  /**

427	   * that owns a directory contributes it as an effect instead of a deployment
428	   * repeating it in configuration.

431	   */
432	  protect(path: string): () => void {
433	    const directory = absoluteDirectory(path, 'protect path')

435	    // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-misused-promises -- synchronous cleanup; direct return preserves disposer identity
436	    return this.ctx.effect(() => {

474	    return this.ctx.effect(() => {

495	      return () => { this.unenforceable.delete(registration) }

509	    if (this.roleOf(session) !== 'implementer') return undefined

513	  /**

526	  /**
527	   * Resolve the complete policy for one capability call. A session whose preset
528	   * declared a role holds that role; otherwise a session holding a reservation
529	   * is the implementer, and every other session and every agentless call is
530	   * unrestricted.
531	   * @param request - the calling session, when there is one.
532	   * @returns the role, the barrier root, and every denied directory.
533	   */
534	  resolve(request: ReadBarrierRequest = {}): ReadBarrierPolicy {
535	    return {
536	      role: this.roleOf(request.session),
537	      root: this.root,
538	      denied: [...new Set([this.root, ...this.configuredDenyRoots, ...this.protectedRoots.values()])],
539	    }
540	  }

542	  /** The role one session holds: the preset's declaration first, then the reservation. */
543	  private roleOf(session: Session | undefined): ReadBarrierRole {
544	    if (session === undefined) return 'unrestricted'
545	    const declared = this.compositions.get(session.id)?.role
546	    if (declared !== undefined) return declared
547	    return this.reservations.has(session.id) ? 'implementer' : 'unrestricted'
548	  }

550	  /**
551	   * One entry per path-opening capability: `denied-at-executor` when the
552	   * capability registered enforcement — through {@link enforce}, or through
553	   * {@link enforceByRefusal} under a `process` or `host` claim — `unenforced`
554	   * when it is composed without one, and `not-composed` when this composition
555	   * does not have it. An `unenforced` entry carries the reason whenever a
556	   * registration supplied one.
557	   * @returns the enforcement census in the fixed capability order.
558	   */
559	  enforcementCensus(): ReadBarrierEnforcementEntry[] {
560	    const enforced = new Set(this.enforcing.values())
561	    const refusing = new Set(this.refusing.values())
562	    const reasons = new Map([...this.unenforceable.values()].map(entry => [entry.capability, entry.reason]))
563	    return Object.entries(ENFORCED_CAPABILITY_SERVICES).map(([name, service]) => {
564	      const capability = name as ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability
565	      if (enforced.has(capability)) return { capability, state: 'denied-at-executor' as const }
566	      if (refusing.has(capability)) {
567	        return this.isolationClaim === 'none'
568	          ? { capability, state: 'unenforced' as const, reason: unclaimedRefusalReason(this.isolationClaim) }
569	          : { capability, state: 'denied-at-executor' as const }
570	      }
571	      // A recorded reason proves the capability is composed: only the
572	      // capability itself registers one, so it outranks the service lookup.
573	      const reason = reasons.get(capability)
574	      if (reason !== undefined) return { capability, state: 'unenforced' as const, reason }
575	      if (this.ctx.get(service) === undefined) return { capability, state: 'not-composed' as const }
576	      return { capability, state: 'unenforced' as const }
577	    })
578	  }

580	  /**
581	   * One census entry per tool the agent's registry view resolves, with the
582	   * authorities each declares, sorted by tool name: the registry answers in
583	   * mount order, which follows concurrent Loader mounts and would make two runs
584	   * of one composition record different censuses.
585	   */
586	  private toolCensus(agent: Agent): ReadBarrierCensusEntry[] {
587	    const tools = agent.ctx.get('tools')
588	    if (tools === undefined) return []
589	    return tools.schemas(agent)
590	      .map(schema => ({
591	        name: schema.name,
592	        authority: [...tools.get(schema.name, agent)?.authority ?? []],
593	      }))

598	  /**

602	   * model.
603	   */
604	  private recordScope(agent: Agent): void {
605	    if (this.censused.has(agent.id)) return
606	    this.censused.add(agent.id)
607	    const composition = this.compositions.get(agent.id)
608	    const scope: ReadBarrierScope = {
609	      version: READ_BARRIER_SCOPE_VERSION,
610	      role: this.roleOf(agent.session),
611	      ...composition === undefined ? {} : { presetId: composition.presetId },
612	      root: this.root,
613	      denied: this.resolve({ session: agent.session }).denied,
614	      census: this.toolCensus(agent),
615	      enforcement: this.enforcementCensus(),
616	    }
617	    agent.session.append('read-barrier/scope', scope)
618	    const attestation = this.verifiedAttestation()
619	    /* v8 ignore start -- only a file owned by another operating-system account reaches this append,
620	       which an unprivileged test process cannot create; `attestationProblem` covers every decision
621	       the record depends on. */
622	    if (attestation !== undefined) agent.session.append('read-barrier/attestation', attestation)
623	    /* v8 ignore stop */
624	  }

626	  /**
627	   * Verify the configured host attestation file.
628	   * @returns the record to append, or undefined when no file is configured, it
629	   * cannot be read, or it does not prove another account owns it.
630	   */
631	  private verifiedAttestation(): ReadBarrierAttestation | undefined {
632	    const path = this.hostAttestation
633	    if (path === undefined) return undefined
634	    let file: AttestationFile
635	    try {
636	      const stats = statSync(path)
637	      file = {
638	        uid: stats.uid,
639	        mode: stats.mode,
640	        isFile: stats.isFile(),
641	        sha256: createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(path)).digest('hex'),
642	      }
643	    } catch {
644	      // An absent or unreadable attestation file is simply no attestation: the
645	      // claim it would have supported is refused instead of the run failing.
646	      this.ctx.logger.warn(`read-barrier: host attestation ${path} cannot be read; no certificate may claim host isolation`)
647	      return undefined
648	    }
649	    const problem = attestationProblem(file, process.geteuid?.())
650	    /* v8 ignore start -- the verifying arm needs a file owned by another operating-system account,
651	       which an unprivileged test process cannot create; `attestationProblem` covers every decision
652	       this arm depends on. */
653	    if (problem === undefined) {
654	      return { version: READ_BARRIER_ATTESTATION_VERSION, path, owner: file.uid, sha256: file.sha256 }
655	    }
656	    /* v8 ignore stop */
657	    this.ctx.logger.warn(`read-barrier: host attestation ${path} ${problem}; no certificate may claim host isolation`)
658	    return undefined
659	  }

661	  /**

665	   */

668	    // to the caller's context, so the guard covers exactly this agent and
669	    // unwinds with it.
670	    agent.ctx.get('tools')?.guard(execution => this.guardExecution(agent, execution))

673	  /** Deny one execution whose definition carries an authority this session's role forbids. */
674	  private guardExecution(agent: Agent, execution: Readonly<ToolExecution>): string | undefined {
675	    const definition = agent.ctx.get('tools')?.get(execution.name, agent)
676	    const role = this.roleOf(agent.session)

681	  /**
682	   * Decide whether the policy denies reading one resolved target. Each denied
683	   * directory is canonicalized through the filesystem seam immediately before
684	   * its containment test, so an ancestor symlink swapped since the target was
685	   * resolved is caught. A target whose containment cannot be decided is denied.
686	   * @param policy - the policy {@link resolve} returned for this call.
687	   * @param target - the already-resolved target the caller is about to read.
688	   * @returns true when the read must be refused.
689	   */
690	  async denies(policy: ReadBarrierPolicy, target: FsTarget): Promise<boolean> {
691	    for (const denied of deniedReadRoots(policy)) {
692	      let directory: FsTarget
693	      try {
694	        directory = await this.ctx.fs.resolve(denied)
695	      } catch {
696	        // A denied directory the backend cannot resolve leaves containment
697	        // undecidable, and an undecidable read fails closed.
698	        return true
699	      }
700	      if (this.ctx.fs.contains(directory, target)) return true
701	    }
702	    return false
703	  }

705	  /**

707	   * every seam that refuses produces the same evidence.
708	   * @param session - the refused session, whose log receives the record.
709	   * @param policy - the policy that refused, supplying the role and root.
710	   * @param capability - the seam that refused the read.
711	   * @param target - the refused target, supplying the model-facing path.
712	   * @returns the payload exactly as it was appended.
713	   */
714	  recordDenial(
715	    session: Session,
716	    policy: ReadBarrierPolicy,
717	    capability: ReadBarrierCapability,
718	    target: FsTarget,
719	  ): ReadBarrierDenial {
720	    const denial: ReadBarrierDenial = {
721	      version: READ_BARRIER_DENIED_VERSION,
722	      role: policy.role,
723	      capability,
724	      displayPath: target.displayPath,
725	      root: policy.root,
726	    }
727	    session.append('read-barrier/denied', denial)

3	 * capabilities that can refuse a read, the resolved per-session policy, the

12	/**
13	 * Authority a session holds against the barrier. `implementer` and `judge` are
14	 * denied every directory the barrier owns and every declared tool authority —
15	 * the implementer so it cannot read the standard it is measured against, the
16	 * judge so it cannot reach the audited session's log or the check instructions
17	 * behind the evidence it was handed. `validator` and `unrestricted` are denied
18	 * nothing, and `unrestricted` is what a session holds without a reservation.
19	 * Which directories and authorities a role may hold is a security invariant,
20	 * never a deployment choice.
21	 */
22	export type ReadBarrierRole = 'implementer' | 'judge' | 'validator' | 'unrestricted'

24	/**
25	 * Capability seam that refused one read. Each member names a seam that opens

30	/**

35	export interface ReadBarrierPolicy {
36	  /** Authority the calling session holds. */
37	  readonly role: ReadBarrierRole

41	  readonly denied: readonly string[]

62	/**
63	 * What a preset roster declares about one agent's composition. The roster is
64	 * the only authority that can raise or lower a session's role, because only
65	 * the composition knows which preset was actually mounted.

67	export interface ReadBarrierComposition {
68	  /** Preset the agent joined, recorded verbatim in the scope census. */

70	  /**

78	/**
79	 * Path-opening capability the scope census reports enforcement for. It extends
80	 * {@link ReadBarrierCapability} with the two executors the harness cannot fence
81	 * in-process and must therefore refuse to start instead of denying a read.
82	 */
83	export type ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability = ReadBarrierCapability | 'subagent' | 'workflow'
84	
85	/**
86	 * What one path-opening capability does about the barrier in this composition:
87	 * it denies at the operation that opens paths, it is composed and denies
88	 * nothing, or the composition does not have it at all.
89	 */
90	export type ReadBarrierEnforcementState = 'denied-at-executor' | 'unenforced' | 'not-composed'
91	
92	/** One capability's enforcement decision, as the scope census records it. */
93	export interface ReadBarrierEnforcementEntry {
94	  /** The path-opening capability. */
95	  readonly capability: ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability
96	  /** What that capability does about the barrier. */
97	  readonly state: ReadBarrierEnforcementState
98	  /**
99	   * Why a composed capability enforces nothing, absent whenever it does. The
100	   * capability itself supplies it — the host's backend cannot express the
101	   * denial, or the deployment claims an isolation that asks nothing of it — so
102	   * a certificate refused over this census can say what was missing instead of
103	   * only which capability was silent.
104	   */
105	  readonly reason?: string

108	/**
109	 * Isolation a deployment intends its certificates to claim, which decides
110	 * whether a capability that cannot be confined in-process refuses to run or
111	 * merely records that it enforces nothing. It repeats `CertificateIsolation`'s

113	 * package, so the dependency cannot run the other way.
114	 */
115	export type ReadBarrierIsolationClaim = 'none' | 'process' | 'host'
116	
117	/** One visible tool and the authorities its definition declares. */
118	export interface ReadBarrierCensusEntry {
119	  /** Tool name as the session's registry view resolves it. */
120	  readonly name: string
121	  /** Authorities the definition declared, empty for an ordinary tool. */
122	  readonly authority: readonly ToolAuthority[]

125	/**
126	 * The composition one session was granted, as the `read-barrier/scope` event
127	 * carries it. Appended before the session's first `request/header`, so the
128	 * census is the durable answer to what the model could reach, and a tool that
129	 * appears in a later header without appearing here was added after the census.
130	 */
131	export interface ReadBarrierScope {
132	  /** Self-declared payload version. */
133	  readonly version: 1
134	  /** Role the session holds for the whole run. */
135	  readonly role: ReadBarrierRole
136	  /** Preset the session composed, absent when the deployment mounts no roster. */
137	  readonly presetId?: string
138	  /** The barrier root in force. */
139	  readonly root: string
140	  /** Every denied directory at census time. */
141	  readonly denied: readonly string[]
142	  /**
143	   * One entry per tool visible to the agent, sorted by tool name. Registry
144	   * order follows concurrent Loader mounts, which would make two runs of one
145	   * composition record different censuses.
146	   */
147	  readonly census: readonly ReadBarrierCensusEntry[]
148	  /** One entry per path-opening capability, in a fixed capability order. */
149	  readonly enforcement: readonly ReadBarrierEnforcementEntry[]
150	}

152	/**
153	 * One verified host attestation, as the `read-barrier/attestation` event
154	 * carries it. The barrier writes it only after a file at the configured path
155	 * proved to be owned by another account and unwritable by this one, which is
156	 * the property an in-process component cannot produce for itself.
157	 */
158	export interface ReadBarrierAttestation {
159	  /** Self-declared payload version. */
160	  readonly version: 1
161	  /** Absolute path of the verified file. */
162	  readonly path: string
163	  /** Numeric owner of the file, always different from this process's effective uid. */
164	  readonly owner: number
165	  /** SHA-256 hex digest of the verified file's bytes. */
166	  readonly sha256: string
167	}

20	/**

22	 * instruction follows it: no retry of the same call succeeds.
23	 * @param displayPath - the model-facing path of the refused target.
24	 * @returns the exact denial message.

26	export function readBarrierDenialMessage(displayPath: string): string {
27	  return `read denied: "${displayPath}" is validator-owned — it is not part of this task; continue without it`

30	/**
31	 * Find the session a read runs for by narrowing the opaque event actor.
32	 * @param actor - the tool-execution context the read executor dispatched with.
33	 * @returns the calling session, or `undefined` for a call with no agent.
34	 */
35	function sessionOf(actor: object | undefined): Session | undefined {
36	  // tsgolint treats object as assignable to weak FsReadBarrierActor, while tsc still requires the structural cast for property access.
37	  // See the analyzer-divergence consequence in .agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-29-oxlint-linter.md.
38	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-unnecessary-type-assertion -- The analyzers disagree on this weak type.

43	export const name = 'fs-read-barrier'

45	/** The barrier owns every deployment-varying value this plugin decides from. */
46	export const inject = ['readBarrier']

48	/**
49	 * Decide one dispatched read.
50	 * @param ctx - the plugin context carrying the barrier service.
51	 * @param target - the resolved target the executor is about to read.
52	 * @param actor - the opaque tool-execution context.
53	 * @returns the refusal, or `undefined` to delegate to the next read policy.
54	 */
55	async function decide(ctx: Context, target: FsTarget, actor: object | undefined): Promise<FsReadDenial | undefined> {
56	  const session = sessionOf(actor)
57	  if (session === undefined) return undefined
58	  const policy = ctx.readBarrier.resolve({ session })
59	  if (!await ctx.readBarrier.denies(policy, target)) return undefined
60	  const denial = ctx.readBarrier.recordDenial(session, policy, 'fs', target)
61	  return { code: 'FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED', message: readBarrierDenialMessage(denial.displayPath) }
62	}

64	/**
65	 * Register the `fs/read-intent` listener.
66	 * @param ctx - the plugin context; the registration is an effect scoped to it.
67	 */
68	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
69	  // Delegating, not single-slot: a barrier that owned the slot would stop every
70	  // later read policy from deciding. The waterfall is unbound (the executor
71	  // dispatches it with no `this`), so the listener takes the raw arguments.
72	  ctx.on('fs/read-intent', async (target, actor, next) => await decide(ctx, target, actor) ?? await next())
73	  // What makes the scope census report `fs` as `denied-at-executor`: the
74	  // registration lives exactly as long as the listener above.
75	  ctx.readBarrier.enforce('fs')
76	}

94	  // Inline schema call: the config catalog walks `static Config` statically.
95	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({

1	/**
2	 * The registration every sandbox-consuming executor makes with the read
3	 * barrier. A capability may claim `denied-at-executor` only when its own
4	 * confinement really would deny the barrier's directories on this host, so the
5	 * registration probes the SAME wrap the executor performs for a real call and
6	 * records why it cannot whenever that wrap refuses.
7	 *
8	 * It lives beside the policy the executors already resolve here because the
9	 * decision needs both halves — the deployment's sandbox mode and the barrier's
10	 * denied set — and duplicating it per executor would let one of them claim an
11	 * enforcement its own backend never applies.
12	 *
13	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-policy/read-barrier
14	 */
15	
16	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
17	import type { SandboxPolicy } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox'
18	import type { ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'
19	
20	/** Why an executor running under the unconfining mode denies nothing. */
21	const FULL_ACCESS = 'the deployment sandbox mode is danger-full-access, which runs commands unconfined'
22	
23	/**
24	 * Register `capability`'s read-barrier enforcement once the barrier is
25	 * composed, deciding between `denied-at-executor` and a reasoned `unenforced`
26	 * by probing this host's confinement.
27	 *
28	 * The probe carries the barrier's own root as the denied directory: it always
29	 * exists and is always denied to an implementer, so a backend that can express
30	 * it can express every other directory the barrier collects.
31	 *
32	 * The registration waits for all three of `readBarrier`, `sandboxPolicy`, and
33	 * `sandbox`, and unwinds with any of them: Loader siblings mount concurrently,
34	 * so probing before the provider exists would record a claim about a
35	 * confinement that was merely late. A composition missing one of the three
36	 * registers nothing, which the census already reports as `unenforced`.
37	 *
38	 * @param ctx - the executor's plugin context.
39	 * @param capability - the path-opening capability this executor provides.
40	 * @param wrap - performs one representative confinement under the probe policy,
41	 *   through the injected scope so the provider resolves without a second
42	 *   declaration; it must throw exactly when this host cannot confine that
43	 *   policy, which is what the executor's own calls would do.
44	 */
45	export function enforceReadBarrier(
46	  ctx: Context,
47	  capability: ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability,
48	  wrap: (policy: SandboxPolicy, scope: Context) => void,
49	): void {
50	  ctx.inject(['readBarrier', 'sandboxPolicy', 'sandbox'], (scope: Context) => {
51	    const barrier = scope.readBarrier
52	    const policy = scope.sandboxPolicy.resolve()
53	    if (policy.mode === 'danger-full-access') {
54	      barrier.cannotEnforce(capability, FULL_ACCESS)
55	      return
56	    }
57	    try {
58	      wrap({ ...policy, mode: policy.mode, deniedReadRoots: [barrier.root] }, scope)
59	    } catch (error: unknown) {
60	      barrier.cannotEnforce(capability, error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error))
61	      return
62	    }
63	    barrier.enforce(capability)
64	  })
65	}
